title: Should the client build, partner or buy? Weigh speed, cost and control to choose the route in
description: How to get into a new market or capability.
hook: When a client wants a new capability or a way into a new market, there are three routes: build it, partner for it, or buy it. Here is a simple comparison you can talk through in a case.
body:
When it helps

How to get into a new market or capability.

The comparison

RouteGood becauseWatch out for
Build (organic)Full control; no integration or culture clashSlow; needs skills the client may not have
Partner (JV, alliance)Shared risk and cost; fast accessShared control and profit
Buy (acquire)Fastest; brings customers and skillsExpensive; integration and culture risk

An example

A UK supermarket wants to offer pharmacy services. Build: hire pharmacists and fit out counters. Slow, but full control. Partner: let an existing pharmacy chain run counters inside its stores. Fast and low risk, but the profit is shared. Buy: acquire a pharmacy chain. Fastest, but expensive and hard to integrate. Which is best depends on how fast they need it and how much they want to own the customer relationship.

How it sounds in an interview

There are three ways in: build it, partner for it, or buy it. I'd choose based on speed, cost and how much control we need. Can I check how quickly the client wants this?

Use it lightly

Treat this as a prompt for your own thinking, not a script. Pick the parts that matter for this client, say why, and leave the rest out. A short, relevant list beats a complete one every time.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. All of these sit on the free frameworks page, next to the 11 core trees.
